text: {"side":"artifact","claims":[{"text":"Blend contamination is the strongest non-astrophysical candidate: 534 of 1461 trigger points (about 37%) are flagged BLEND_SUSPECT, and the listed 1930s to 1950s dips (e.g., offsets of -1.071, -1.150, -1.027, -1.115 mag) all carry that tag, so a neighbouring star or overlapping image could produce deep apparent drops.","evidence_ids":["E-060","E-047","E-049","E-051","E-054"]},{"text":"Several of the deepest dips also carry SHAPE_OUTLIER tags, which is consistent with a blended or distorted image rather than a real stellar change; 353 of 1461 points are shape outliers overall.","evidence_ids":["E-062","E-048","E-049","E-050","E-051","E-055"]},{"text":"Plate-edge and emulsion problems are present in the trigger: 75 points are flagged plate_edge, 63 emulsion_non_blue and 3 emulsion_unknown, so edge vignetting or emulsion response differences could shift magnitudes on the affected plates.","evidence_ids":["E-063","E-058","E-059"]},{"text":"The dip is tied to the 1930s to 1950s period, when the decade median offsets drift negative (-0.001 in the 1930s, -0.134 in the 1940s, -0.388 in the 1950s) and the series zero points for rh (-0.101) and rl (-0.247) are offset from the early-century series; a calibration or series-seam effect is a plausible source of a long-term apparent trend.","evidence_ids":["E-009","E-010","E-011","E-040","E-041"]},{"text":"The packet does not rule out an artifact: the event rests on a single long-term candidate with 30 of 1461 points shown, the amplitude is 0.74 mag, the L2 score is only an ordering value, and the packet gives no per-plate image checks or star-field overlays that would separate a blend from a real change, so these checks are missing and should be requested.","evidence_ids":["E-002","E-003","E-057"]}]}
